Bayesian Accuracy of Multiple Diagnostic Tests under Partial Verification

Source: R/baysesp-package.R
baysesp-package.Rd

{baysesp} estimates the sensitivity, specificity and predictive values of one or more binary diagnostic tests performed on the same subjects, when the disease status is ascertained by the reference standard only for a subset of them. Verification that depends on the test results produces verification bias if it is ignored (Begg and Greenes, 1983). The package takes a Bayesian approach, which places priors on the parameters that are not identified (Buzoianu and Kadane, 2008). The models are computed in Stan (Carpenter et al., 2017).

References

Begg, C. B. and Greenes, R. A. (1983). Assessment of diagnostic tests when disease verification is subject to selection bias. Biometrics, 39(1), 207–215. doi:10.2307/2530820

Buzoianu, M. and Kadane, J. B. (2008). Adjusting for verification bias in diagnostic test evaluation: A Bayesian approach. Statistics in Medicine, 27(13), 2453–2473. doi:10.1002/sim.3099

Carpenter, B., Gelman, A., Hoffman, M. D., Lee, D., Goodrich, B., Betancourt, M., Brubaker, M., Guo, J., Li, P. and Riddell, A. (2017). Stan: A probabilistic programming language. Journal of Statistical Software, 76(1), 1–32. doi:10.18637/jss.v076.i01
